angle:
Runtime level: the Vitest and Playwright configuration on this 4-CPU host. I read it from code and from the live journey-6 run, which started at 02:31:51 and read 858.59 s with 4 failed, 86 passed, 6 skipped, and 2493.59 s summed (tmp/units/tokens-t3/journey-6.log:203-205).

What the configuration does today:
- Projects: the four variant projects share execution group 1 (configs/app/vite.journey.config.ts:10-15, 45). The browser pool starts every project's pool at once (node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/cli-api.CnMVyzaz.js:2448-2476) and ignores the group's `maxWorkers` value of 3 (3832-3838). Each pool gets one worker because the `fileParallelism` setting is false (vite.config.ts:327; cli-api.CnMVyzaz.js:2482-2486). Each project therefore runs one tester iframe, with its cases in series.
- Browsers: the provider is built per project (node_modules/@vitest/browser-playwright/dist/index.js:825-830) and launches its own Chromium (941). The run holds 4 browser, 4 GPU, 4 network-service, and 4 renderer processes. Playwright 1.63's pinned path /opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome is absent, so `resolveManagedBrowser` returns the /opt/pw-browsers/chromium alias (configs/browsers.ts:164, 309). That alias is the full chromium-1194 binary, launched with --headless, --disable-dev-shm-usage, and --num-raster-threads=2 (live command lines).
- Viewport: the context sets no viewport (index.js:1080-1086), so each iframe sits in Playwright's 1280x720 page. The orchestrator scales it by min(1, 1280/width, 720/height): 0.9 at 1280x800 and 390x800, and 0.853 at 390x844 (node_modules/@vitest/browser/dist/client/__vitest_browser__/orchestrator-jtzFEKPy.js:399-410).
- Budgets: no `testTimeout` value is set (vite.config.ts:298-332, 398-424), so cases without a budget get 15 s (journey-5.err:14). The `screenshotFailures` option resolves to true (node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/coverage.DM_a_rWm.js:519), and every failure sits in light-390 or dark-390, off the critical path.
- Host load, sampled during journey-6 with ps and /proc:
  - The renderers used 68.8 to 79.4 percent of a core at 447 s and 52.3 to 81.9 percent at 773 s.
  - Supporting processes used little: GPU 3.7 to 5.9 percent, browser 1.2 to 2.3, network service 0.2 to 0.4, and the Vitest process 7.1 to 9.5.
  - The host was saturated: load average 9.81 on 4 CPUs, /proc/pressure/cpu some avg300 52.20, and vmstat idle 13 to 14 percent.
  - Renderer RSS read 1,070,052 to 1,775,380 KB.

Finding: the configuration already runs at the host's parallel ceiling, which is four single-threaded renderer main threads on four CPUs. The wall is light-1280's serial work. In the 591.13 s run it ends at 591.12 s while dark-1280, light-390, and dark-390 end at 476.86, 465.02, and 396.97 s (journey-4.json:1). Those three projects therefore sit idle for 114.26, 126.10, and 194.15 s at the end of the run. Light-1280's four logged bodies sum to 318.05 s in the 761.76 s run (journey-5b.log:17, 59, 139, 195) and to 395.56 s in journey-6 (journey-6.log:13, 59, 151, 199). The runtime lever that moves the wall is filling that idle tail through the four projects' schedule (changes 3 and 4). No flag adds a renderer or cuts renderer work without changing a reading.

Rulings on the runtime options:
1. A fifth concurrent project, or `fileParallelism` with a split file: refuse. Each adds a renderer to 4 CPUs at load average 9.81, plus about 1.5 to 2.2 GB, against J0c's peak of 12,288,905,216 bytes under a 14,345,035,776-byte cap (j0c-report.md:117).
2. Concurrency inside a project: refuse. The cases share one document and the portfolio sets (integration.test.ts:165-168, 1855, 1884).
3. One browser shared by the four projects through `PLAYWRIGHT_WS_ENDPOINT` (configs/browsers.ts:299-301): refuse. It removes three browser processes at 1.2 to 2.3 percent of a core each. The GPU compositing moves to one process rather than disappearing, and every CDP command gains a WebSocket hop.
4. One browser context for the four variants: refuse. Contexts are keyed per provider and session (index.js:1073-1092), and one context means one orchestrator running the variants in series.
5. The headless shell build (/opt/pw-browsers/chromium_headless_shell-1194): refuse. It saves part of 1.2 to 2.3 percent of a core per browser and re-baselines every reading and the host-bound set against another build (lanes.md:52).
6. Unthrottled frames, CDP animation playback rate, or virtual time: refuse. The motion=true rows prove real transitions, and J0c phase 1 cut idle waits without moving the wall (j0c-scope.md:32).
7. Force clicks or skipped actionability checks: refuse, because they drop the reachability proof each click carries.
8. Raising light-1280's CPU priority with nice or chrt: refuse. It takes CPU from light-390 and dark-390, which hold every host-bound title (lanes.md:58), and change 4 makes it unnecessary.
9. Budget changes: keep every budget. A budget does not change a passing run's wall. Each budget still has room:
   - Paired engine: 93.44 of 120 s (flip-gates-2/test:journey.log:59; integration.test.ts:1000).
   - Preservation: 150.93 of 300 s (flip-gates-2/test:journey.log:135; integration.test.ts:1438).
   - Component tables: at least 225 s (10,000 ms plus 2,500 ms times a largest row count of at least 86, journey-5b.err data-statechart-total; integration.test.ts:1834), against 82.37 s for scrollspy-390 motion=true.
   - The 15 s defaults: at most 3.41 s used (journey-4.json:1).
10. Start-up offsets: leave them. They read 10.29, 15.54, 16.26, and 16.53 s, with setup 6.49 s and import 2.81 s summed (journey-4.json:1; journey-4.log:169), and cutting them needs Vitest internals.

On the user's question about parallelism: four renderers is the ceiling inside the gate. Across lanes, other lanes can keep doing agent work beside the gate, but their CPU-bound commands run at nice 19 and their Chromium suites wait on the journey lock (change 2).

changes.change: Add the JSON reporter beside the dot reporter in the gate script, writing the report to `tmp/journey/report.json`. J0c ran the same form (`--reporter=dot --reporter=json --outputFile=...`, j0c-brief.md:89).
changes.basis: The dot reporter prints no per-case duration. In the 761.76 s run only ten bodies carry a logged time (journey-5b.log:13-19, 59, 79, 125, 139, 195), and 234.95 s of summed growth cannot be attributed to any case. The JSON report records every case's duration and each project's startTime and endTime (journey-4.json:1, 36,960 bytes). Changes 3 and 4 are planned from those values.
changes.coverage_kept_how: The change touches only the reporter. No test, assertion, or reading changes, and the dot output and its logged lines stay.
changes.risk: No reading is affected. The file lands in the ignored tmp directory (.gitignore:11).

changes.change: Give the gate the host. Wrap `npm run test:journey` and every Chromium suite in `flock /home/user/.wave/journey.lock`, the rule J0c ran under (j0c-brief.md:22). While the lock is held, run every other lane's CPU-bound command (check, vue-tsc, build, lint:check, format:check, and the Node Vitest projects) under `nice -n 19`. Lanes keep doing agent work beside the gate.
changes.files: No veneer file changes. The change is the dispatch brief and launch line of every lane that shares this host, for example `launch.js ... -- flock /home/user/.wave/journey.lock npm run test:journey`.
changes.basis: No saving is claimed against 761.76 s, because nothing outside the T3 unit folder wrote a file during that run (find over /home/user and /root/.claude/projects, 2026-10-05 00:02:46 to 00:15:28). journey-6 ran without the lock: process 7881 launched `npm run test:journey` with no flock in its command. It overlapped the T4 lane's acceptance checks from 02:39:16 to 02:44:04 (/home/user/.wave/veneer-t4/tmp/units/tokens-t4/acceptance/*.log and acceptance-final/*.log). The sample taken during that overlap read vue-tsc at 63.4 percent of a core, load average 9.81 on 4 CPUs, /proc/pressure/cpu some avg300 52.20, and vmstat idle 13 to 14 percent. journey-6 read 858.59 s (journey-6.log:205), but its J4 and paired bodies ran before the T4 checks began, and the sixth pass changed the partition control, so this run cannot isolate the overlap's cost. The kernel scheduler weights a nice 19 task at 15 against 1024 for nice 0, so a niced check mostly uses the CPU the four renderers leave idle.
changes.coverage_kept_how: No test changes. Run contention stays at the four-project level under which the host-bound set was recorded (lanes.md:50-58), so overlapping lanes cannot add a failing title outside that set.
changes.risk: Other lanes' Chromium suites wait for the lock, and niced commands slow down while the gate runs. Chromium suites stay serialized because a fifth browser adds about 1.5 to 2.2 GB, measured from live renderer RSS plus the browser, GPU, and network processes. That is too much against J0c's peak of 12,288,905,216 bytes under a 14,345,035,776-byte cap (j0c-report.md:117).

changes.change: Split the preservation case (integration.test.ts:1123-1439) and the partition case (1441-1695) into one registration per width. Place each 390 half in a project with idle time: preservation at 390 in dark-390, and partition at 390 in light-390. Each half reads the light-1280 variant object with its width replaced, as the loops do today (`{ ...OWN, width }`, 1131, 1447). Record the placement in a frozen object beside `JOURNEY_PLACEMENTS` (setupBrowser.ts:5339-5345), and register the halves with `it.each` filtered to `VARIANT`, as the shared cases do (integration.test.ts:459, 686).
changes.files: tests/app/browser/integration.test.ts:1123-1439 and 1441-1695: the two `it.skipIf(VARIANT !== 'light-1280')` registrations and their width loops at 1129 and 1446. tests/setupBrowser.ts:5339-5345: the placement record.
changes.basis:
The model works from the 761.76 s run:
- Preservation at 390: the scan reads 33.00 s (journey-5b.log:127), and controls and builds take 71.17 s of the 135.43 s both widths share (journey-5b.log:97, 139). The 390 half is therefore about 68.6 s.
- Partition reads 84.29 s for both widths (journey-5b.log:195), about 42.1 s per width.
- Project spans come from journey-4.json:1 per case. Untimed cases are scaled by 1.159, which is the 234.95 s of unattributed growth over the 1479.03 s those cases summed in the 591.13 s run. That gives light-1280 735.5 s, dark-1280 535.7, light-390 518.9, and dark-390 439.8.
- After the split, light-1280 drops to 624.8 s, light-390 rises to 561.0, and dark-390 to 508.4. Light-1280's end, with its 10.29 s offset, moves from about 745.8 s to about 635.1 s.
- In journey-6 the two cases grew to 148.99 and 143.16 s (journey-6.log:151, 199), so the split saves more on the landed tree.
changes.coverage_kept_how:
Each half runs the same body for its width: the tuned-sheet parse, 1458 signatures, the readings under both faces, the three attributions (1215, 1273-1276, 1282-1285), the three sheet-rewrite controls (1314-1426), the three full partitions and the subset partitions, the adopted control sheets, and the map and role controls. The reading geometry is unchanged:
- `buildJourney` sets the viewport on every build (setupBrowser.ts:1157), and the orchestrator resizes the iframe on that command (orchestrator-jtzFEKPy.js:292-312).
- Every project's page is Playwright's 1280x720 default (browser-playwright index.js:1080-1086), so a 390x800 reading scales by min(1, 1280/390, 720/800) = 0.9 in any project, the same as in light-1280 (orchestrator-jtzFEKPy.js:399-410).
- `applyTheme('light-1280')` selects the light theme (setupBrowser.ts:1159).
The rows land in the host project's journey file (integration.test.ts:1242, 1551, 1859-1880), so prefix each row with the reading's variant and width. Each half keeps the 300 s budget; both widths together read 150.93 s in the 895.58 s run (flip-gates-2/test:journey.log:135).
changes.risk: The host project's renderer holds the 10225-element readings at the same time as light-1280 holds its own, so the two memory peaks overlap. Sample memory against the cap. The six skipped registrations disappear and the registered count changes, so acceptance compares titles, not counts. light-390 and dark-390 hold the host-bound titles, so confirm the failing set stays inside lanes.md:58.

changes.change: Rebalance three component tables through their `variant` fields. The paired-engine family follows each table, because the paired case iterates its variant's tables (integration.test.ts:864). Move alert from light-1280 to dark-390 (setupBrowser.ts:5361), modal from light-1280 to dark-1280 (5431), and dropdown from dark-1280 to light-1280 (5389). Keep J0c's constraints (j0c-brief.md:217-218): modal and offcanvas stay at 1280, and scrollspy, navbar, and responsive-offcanvas keep their widths. Keep every host-bound table and case where lanes.md:58 records it: accordion and J8 in light-390; tooltip, collapse, and navbar-390 in dark-390; and the shared J7, J8, and frozen pair in dark-1280 and light-390.
changes.basis:
Per-case seconds come from journey-4.json:1, scaled by 1.159:
- Alert: 30.64 s becomes 35.5.
- Modal: 56.12 s becomes 65.0.
- Dropdown: 42.63 s becomes 49.4.
- Paired families: about 85.83/5 and 82.27/6 s each (journey-5b.log:59, 125).
After change 3, the projects become:
- light-1280: 624.8 - 50 (alert) - 82 (modal) + 63 (dropdown) = 555.9 s.
- dark-1280: 535.7 + 82 - 63 = 554.6 s.
- light-390: 561.0 s.
- dark-390: 508.4 + 50 = 558.4 s.
With start offsets of 10.29, 15.54, 16.26, and 16.53 s (journey-4.json:1), the last project ends near 577.3 s, against about 635.1 s after change 3 alone.
changes.coverage_kept_how: Every row of each moved table runs in its new project. Modal and dropdown stay at width 1280, so `clickDialogBackdrop` keeps its backdrop point (j0c-brief.md:218). Each moved family keeps its three-face paired reading and its 'engine <family>: three equal faces' row (integration.test.ts:986). For each moved table, show one mutation red in its new project and green after restore, as J0c proved toast in dark-390 (j0c-report.md:63-79).
changes.risk: Alert crosses from 1280 to 390. If a row fails at 390 outside the host-bound set, keep alert at 1280 in dark-1280 and re-plan. The uniform 1.159 scale is an assumption, so the change 1 baseline decides the final moves, with the fewest moves first.

changes.change: Run the gate with `TMPDIR=/dev/shm`, kept only if it shows a measured gain.
changes.files: package.json:101 (the `test:journey` script) or the launch command
changes.basis: No saving is claimed. Playwright passes --disable-dev-shm-usage to every Chromium it launches (node_modules/playwright-core/lib/coreBundle.js:53; live command line) and places profiles under /tmp/playwright_chromiumdev_profile-*. /tmp sits on the ext4 root /dev/vda, while /dev/shm is a 16 GB tmpfs with 0 used (df). Under that flag, Chromium might take its shared-memory files from TMPDIR or /tmp. vmstat during journey-6 read 292 to 588 blocks out per second, with ext4 writeback workers active.
changes.coverage_kept_how: No reading observes where a profile or shared-memory file lives, and no test changes.
changes.risk: tmpfs pages count as memory, replacing page-cache pages the same files held. A gain smaller than the run-to-run spread cannot be read from 2 runs per arm.

target_basis:
The target is modeled on the tree of the 761.76 s run.
- The summed test time is 2231.49 s (journey-5b.log:201), so a perfect four-way split gives 557.87 s per project.
- Changes 3 and 4 put the four spans at 555.9, 554.6, 561.0, and 558.4 s. With the measured start offsets of 10.29 to 16.53 s (journey-4.json:1), the last project ends near 577 s.
- Add about 10 s. In that run, light-1280's last 200 s or so ran with fewer projects beside it, and after the moves that work runs under four-way load. Four-way contention adds 15 to 21 percent to J4 and 37 to 43 percent to the scan cases, compared with running alone (j4-5-isolated.log:9, paired-5.log:19, and preservation-5b.log:29, against journey-5b.log:13-19, 59, 139).
- That gives 590 s, down from 761.76 s. The gain comes from the schedule, not the flags: the configuration already runs at four renderers on four CPUs.

On the landed token tree, re-derive the target from the instrumented baseline the same way: summed test time over four, plus the largest start offset, plus the tail allowance. For journey-6's tree (2493.59 s summed, journey-6.log:205), that rule gives about 650 s against 858.59 s.
measurement_plan:
Before:
1. On the landed token tree, give the gate the host (change 2).
2. Run the gate twice with the JSON reporter (change 1) and the J0b sampler (tmp/codex/j0b-measure.ts). Extend the sampler to record /proc/loadavg and /proc/pressure/cpu with each memory sample.
3. Record, per project, the start offset and span (testResults[i].startTime and endTime). Also record every case's duration, the summed test time, the failing titles, and peak memory.
4. Re-plan changes 3 and 4 from those per-case durations. Choose the fewest moves that bring every project's offset plus span within the target, under change 4's constraints.
5. Treat a run as host-loaded and rerun it when a sample shows a CPU-bound process outside the gate at default priority. Same-tree runs on this host have read 761.76 s and 895.58 s (journey-5b.log:201; flip-gates-2/test:journey.log:201), so one run per arm decides nothing.

After: take two consecutive full runs under the same conditions. Success needs all of the following.
- The failing titles are a subset of the host-bound set (lanes.md:58), and every host-bound title stays registered in its recorded variant. The failing subset varies within that set from run to run: J8, accordion, and navbar-390 in the 761.76 s run (journey-5b.err:10, 27, 48); J8, accordion, tooltip, and collapse in the 858.59 s run (journey-6.err:13, 30, 61, 82); and J8, accordion, and collapse in the 895.58 s run (flip-gates-2/test:journey.err:10, 27, 52). Compare against the set, not against one run.
- Every baseline case title runs, with preservation and partition each split into one title per width.
- Each width's logged readings equal the baseline's. On the 761.76 s tree those are 10225 elements, 1458 signatures, 9704 and 9526 boxes, 0 preflight, and 0 unattributed (journey-5b.log:97, 127). Partition reads 8271 elements, 1670 signatures, and 209 names with empty violations (journey-5b.log:149, 159, 175, 181). Each family has one 'engine <family>: three equal faces' row across the four tmp/journey files.
- Each moved table and each moved half reads red under one mutation in its new project, then green after restore.
- In both runs, the wall reads at or under the target and every project's offset plus span fits within it.
- Peak memory stays under 14,345,035,776 bytes.

For change 5, alternate 2 runs with TMPDIR=/dev/shm and 2 without on the landed schedule. Keep it only when both runs with it read a lower summed test time than both runs without it; otherwise drop it.
